persona_texts: Mei Chen is a 24-year-old international student from Guangzhou, China, enrolled full-time in a Master of Education at Monash University and living in a four-person share house in Clayton, Melbourne. She speaks Mandarin, Cantonese and English, works part-time in hospitality and retail, and is cost-sensitive but generous with communal meals. As an ENFJ, she is highly extraverted, community-minded and consensus-driven; she organises house dinners, mediates disputes and keeps the group connected through Telegram and X, though she is also cautious about personal safety, verifies people before trusting them, and is sceptical of strong data-privacy restrictions. Outwardly calm and cheerful, she carries high baseline anxiety and depressive dips, high attachment anxiety and vulnerability, and manages these with an irregular sleep schedule, shift work, occasional meditation, tea rituals and a dog she misses back home. Her conscientiousness is very low in personal admin - she rarely uses to-do lists, budgets or goal setting, and her room is messy - yet she is dutiful about commitments and insists on quality even when moving at speed. She is logical, detail-oriented, modest, assertive and loyal, with strong kindness, fairness, honesty and playfulness, but very low sympathy and empathy in the sense that she does not absorb others' emotions; she acts kindly without becoming emotionally porous. She values family, wealth, personal freedom, adventure, tradition, community, spirituality, social status, helping others and privacy. She prefers city life, outdoor time, one-on-one conversations and hybrid study or work; she is an Apple and Chrome user who pays mostly in cash, is politically centrist and secular while spiritually strong, supports climate action and nuclear energy, is sceptical of renewables, homeownership, free markets, government regulation and electric vehicles, and is positive toward new technology, subscriptions, minimalism, fast fashion and taking on debt. In the share house she is the social glue, but her low follow-through on chores and admin can frustrate housemates.

Arjun Nair is a 23-year-old international student from Kochi, India, studying a Master of Design at Monash University's Caulfield campus and living in the same Clayton share house, commuting by car. He speaks English, Malayalam and Hindi, works part-time in a cafe and as a freelance creative, and is cost-sensitive despite being a free spender on art supplies and experiences. As an ENFP, he is a strong extrovert, highly intuitive, novelty-seeking, competitive, artistic and spiritually devout, with high altruism, modesty, cheerfulness and love of learning. He values health, power, achievement, creativity, social status, independence and helping others; he is autonomous, needs relatedness and competence, and can be directive when leading group projects, though he is usually late, messy in shared spaces and prone to impulse buying. Arjun is risk-averse about safety but excitement-seeking socially, with high negative emotionality, anxiety, depression and attachment anxiety; his mental health is struggling, he has a medical dietary restriction, reduced manual dexterity and mild attention challenges, yet he is highly health-literate and comprehensively insured. He cooks daily, keeps caffeine high, drinks tea rather than coffee, avoids alcohol and smoking, stretches daily, and is a night owl who doomscrolls on YouTube and WhatsApp. He prefers city life, variety, big groups, outdoor time, remote-leaning study and a 9-to-5-style part-time job, though his punctuality is poor. Politically apolitical, he is devout and socially traditional in some ways; he is sceptical of data privacy and new technology, positive toward free markets, government regulation, nuclear energy, homeownership, risk-taking, subscriptions, working from the office and electric vehicles, but sceptical of climate action, consumerism, fast fashion, urban density and privacy-versus-security trade-offs. In the share house he brings energy and big-group social events, but housemates may need to remind him about rent deadlines, cleaning and quiet hours.

Tharindu Jayasuriya is a 27-year-old international student from Colombo, Sri Lanka, completing a PhD in public health at Monash University and living in the Clayton share house. He speaks Sinhala, Tamil and English, works part-time in disability and aged-care support, and is cost-sensitive, practical and routine-oriented. As an ISFJ, he is highly conscientious, dutiful and productively focused, with a strong need for closure, high interpersonal dominance and a habit of always leading. He is devout, community-minded and values wealth, personal freedom, adventure, tradition, achievement, creativity, community, knowledge, social status, recognition, helping others, personal growth, integrity and order. Outwardly he can seem reserved or socially low, yet he is energised by structured group activity and takes charge of bills, rosters and maintenance; he trusts very little, feels highly vulnerable, and becomes frustrated when housemates ignore agreed systems. His risk profile is unusual: he is risk-tolerant overall and very high in health and safety risk tolerance, but very low in financial, ethical and social risk tolerance, and he avoids debt despite being positive toward it in principle. He is reluctant with technology, uses Android, Instagram and Messenger, pays by mobile wallet, walks as his main commute, and keeps a cat at his family home rather than in the rental. He is a remote-leaning flexible worker and student, cooks daily, avoids alcohol, smoking and caffeine, has a slow morning routine, chaotic tidiness, poor sleep, high stress, mild chronic pain, mild mobility limitation, diagnosed attention issues and daily medication. He is also an elder caregiver from a distance, which shapes his yearly planning horizon and his need for stability. He supports data privacy, free markets, government regulation, nuclear energy, new technology, minimalism and public transit, opposes renewable energy and privacy-versus-security trade-offs, and is positive toward electric vehicles. In the share house he is the de facto manager and anchor, but his low trust and high frustration can make him rigid.

Linh Nguyen is a 22-year-old international student from Hanoi, Vietnam, studying a Bachelor of Commerce and Information Technology at Monash University and living in the Clayton share house. She speaks Vietnamese and English, works part-time as an online tutor and freelance analyst, and is cost-sensitive but a frugal saver in practice. As an ISFJ, she is highly conscientious, orderly, dutiful and productive, with a strong need for security, routine, accuracy and quality; she is analytical, competitive, early-adopting in selected technologies, and strongly prefers solo work and structured environments. She is devout, left-leaning, spiritually strong, and values career success, wealth, creativity, community, faith, social status, loyalty, recognition, personal growth, integrity, order, structure and privacy. Beneath a calm exterior she has very high neuroticism, anxiety, anger, depression and emotional volatility, low assertiveness, high warmth, high sympathy and a strong need for relatedness, yet she can be blunt or low in respectfulness when stressed. Her mental health is struggling, her sleep is poor, she has a managed chronic condition, an ethical dietary restriction, low cognitive-load capacity and strong motion sensitivity, so she prefers reduced-motion settings and quiet shared spaces. She never cooks, which makes her dependent on housemates, meal delivery or prepared food, and she is a night owl with more than eight hours of daily screen time, gaming weekly, YouTube and Telegram use, a Windows laptop, Safari browser, mobile wallet and neobank. She is positive toward remote work, office work, risk-taking, new technology, subscription services, homeownership, electric vehicles and urban density, but sceptical of free markets and minimalism and opposed to strong data-privacy restrictions, preferring convenience and security. She volunteers monthly, journals occasionally, keeps to-do lists weekly and is generally on time, but her low resilience and high emotional volatility mean she needs predictable house routines and clear boundaries. In the share house she is the quiet, private anchor who keeps her own space orderly but may struggle with the communal kitchen and noise.
